metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: The LORD’s word that came to Hosea the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.
units.rightText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and of Jeroboam son of Jehoash, king of Israel.
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).
rightNotes: 1:1 Hebrew Joash, a variant of Jehoash

units.leftText: When the LORD spoke at first by Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of unfaithfulness; for the land commits great adultery, forsaking the LORD.”
units.rightText: When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, He told him, “Go, take a prostitute as your wife and have children of adultery, because this land is flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD.”

units.leftText: So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived, and bore him a son.
units.rightText: So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.

units.leftText: The LORD said to him, “Call his name Jezreel, for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Hosea, “Name him Jezreel, for soon I will bring the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.
rightNotes: 1:4 Jezreel means God sows; also in verse 11.

units.leftText: It will happen in that day that I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.”
units.rightText: And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel.”

units.leftText: She conceived again, and bore a daughter. Then he said to him, “Call her name Lo-Ruhamah, for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, that I should in any way pardon them.
units.rightText: Gomer again conceived and gave birth to a daughter, and the LORD said to Hosea, “Name her Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that I should ever forgive them.
rightNotes: 1:6 Lo-ruhamah means she has not received mercy.

units.leftText: But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and will save them by the LORD their God, and will not save them by bow, sword, battle, horses, or horsemen.”
units.rightText: Yet I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them — not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God.”

units.leftText: Now when she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, she conceived, and bore a son.
units.rightText: After she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, Gomer conceived and gave birth to a son.

units.leftText: He said, “Call his name Lo-Ammi, for you are not my people, and I will not be yours.
units.rightText: And the LORD said, “Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I am not your God.
rightNotes: 1:9 Lo-ammi means not My people.
1:9 Hebrew I am not yours

units.leftText: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured or counted; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
units.rightText: Yet the number of the Israelites will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. And it will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
rightNotes: 1:10 Cited in Romans 9:26|ROM 9:26*

units.leftText: The children of Judah and the children of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint themselves one head, and will go up from the land; for great will be the day of Jezreel.
units.rightText: Then the people of Judah and of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint for themselves one leader, and will go up out of the land. For great will be the day of Jezreel.[’’]

units.leftText: “Say to your brothers, ‘My people!’ and to your sisters, ‘My loved one!’
units.rightText: “Say of your brothers, ‘My people,’ and of your sisters, ‘My loved one.’
rightNotes: 2:1 Hebrew Ammi
2:1 Or Mercy is shown; Hebrew Ruhamah, which means she has received mercy

units.leftText: Contend with your mother! Contend, for she is not my wife, neither am I her husband; and let her put away her prostitution from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts;
units.rightText: Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adultery from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.

units.leftText: lest I strip her naked, and make her bare as in the day that she was born, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and kill her with thirst.
units.rightText: Otherwise, I will strip her naked and expose her like the day of her birth. I will make her like a desert and turn her into a parched land, and I will let her die of thirst.

units.leftText: Indeed, on her children I will have no mercy, for they are children of unfaithfulness.
units.rightText: I will have no compassion on her children, because they are the children of adultery.

units.leftText: For their mother has played the prostitute. She who conceived them has done shamefully; for she said, ‘I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink.’
units.rightText: For their mother has played the harlot and has conceived them in disgrace. For she thought, ‘I will go after my lovers, who give me bread and water, wool and linen, oil and drink.’

units.leftText: Therefore behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, that she can’t find her way.
units.rightText: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up her path with thorns; I will enclose her with a wall, so she cannot find her way.
leftNotes: 2:6 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
rightNotes: 2:6 Hebrew your path

units.leftText: She will follow after her lovers, but she won’t overtake them; and she will seek them, but won’t find them. Then she will say, ‘I will go and return to my first husband, for then it was better with me than now.’
units.rightText: She will pursue her lovers but not catch them; she will seek them but not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will return to my first husband, for then I was better off than now.’

units.leftText: For she didn’t know that I gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and multiplied to her silver and gold, which they used for Baal.
units.rightText: For she does not acknowledge that it was I who gave her grain, new wine, and oil, who lavished on her silver and gold — which they crafted for Baal.

units.leftText: Therefore I will take back my grain in its time, and my new wine in its season, and will pluck away my wool and my flax which should have covered her nakedness.
units.rightText: Therefore I will take back My grain in its time and My new wine in its season; I will take away My wool and linen, which were given to cover her nakedness.

units.leftText: Now I will uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of my hand.
units.rightText: And then I will expose her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of My hands.

units.leftText: I will also cause all her celebrations to cease: her feasts, her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her solemn assemblies.
units.rightText: I will put an end to all her exultation: her feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths— all her appointed feasts.

units.leftText: I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, about which she has said, ‘These are my wages that my lovers have given me,’ and I will make them a forest, and the animals of the field shall eat them.
units.rightText: I will destroy her vines and fig trees, which she thinks are the wages paid by her lovers. So I will make them into a thicket, and the beasts of the field will devour them.

units.leftText: I will visit on her the days of the Baals, to which she burned incense when she decked herself with her earrings and her jewels, and went after her lovers and forgot me,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: I will punish her for the days of the Baals when she burned incense to them, when she adorned herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers. But Me she forgot,” declares the LORD. God’s Mercy to Israel

units.leftText: “Therefore behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her.
units.rightText: “Therefore, behold, I will allure her and lead her to the wilderness, and speak to her tenderly.

units.leftText: I will give her vineyards from there, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope; and she will respond there as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: There I will give back her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor into a gateway of hope. There she will respond as she did in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.
rightNotes: 2:15 Achor means trouble.

units.leftText: It will be in that day,” says the LORD, “that you will call me ‘my husband,’ and no longer call me ‘my master.’
units.rightText: In that day,” declares the LORD, “you will call Me ‘my Husband,’ and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’
rightNotes: 2:16 Hebrew my Ishi
2:16 Hebrew my Baal

units.leftText: For I will take away the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and they will no longer be mentioned by name.
units.rightText: For I will remove from her lips the names of the Baals; no longer will their names be invoked.

units.leftText: In that day I will make a covenant for them with the animals of the field, and with the birds of the sky, and with the creeping things of the ground. I will break the bow, the sword, and the battle out of the land, and will make them lie down safely.
units.rightText: On that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground. And I will abolish bow and sword and battle in the land, and will make them lie down in safety.

units.leftText: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion.
units.rightText: So I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in loving devotion and compassion.
rightNotes: 2:19 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know the LORD.
units.rightText: And I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.”

units.leftText: It will happen in that day, that I will respond,” says the LORD. “I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth;
units.rightText: “On that day I will respond —” declares the LORD — “I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth.

units.leftText: and the earth will respond to the grain, and the new wine, and the oil; and they will respond to Jezreel.
units.rightText: And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.
rightNotes: 2:22 Jezreel means God sows.

units.leftText: I will sow her to me in the earth; and I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; and I will tell those who were not my people, ‘You are my people;’ and they will say, ‘You are My God!’”
units.rightText: And I will sow her as My own in the land, and I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’ I will say to those called ‘Not My People,’ ‘You are My people,’ and they will say, ‘You are my God.’”
rightNotes: 2:23 Hebrew Lo-ruhamah; LXX I will love her who was not loved
2:23 Hebrew Lo-ammi
2:23 Cited in Romans 9:25|ROM 9:25* and 1 Peter 2:10

units.leftText: The LORD said to me, “Go again, love a woman loved by another, and an adulteress, even as the LORD loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods, and love cakes of raisins.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to me, “Go show love to your wife again, though she is loved by another and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love to offer raisin cakes to idols. ”
rightNotes: 3:1 Or Go show love to a woman who is loved by another
3:1 Literally and love raisin cakes

units.leftText: So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a half of barley.
units.rightText: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.
leftNotes: 3:2 1 homer is about 220 liters or 6 bushels
rightNotes: 3:2 15 shekels is approximately 6 ounces or 171 grams of silver.

3:2 Or a homer and a half of barley; that is, a total of approximately 9.36 bushels or 330 liters (probably about 436 pounds or 198 kilograms of barley); LXX a homer of barley and a wineskin full of wine

units.leftText: I said to her, “You shall stay with me many days. You shall not play the prostitute, and you shall not be with any other man. I will also be so toward you.”
units.rightText: Then I said to her, “You must live with me for many days; you must not be promiscuous or belong to another, and I will do the same for you.”

units.leftText: For the children of Israel shall live many days without king, without prince, without sacrifice, without sacred stone, and without ephod or idols.
units.rightText: For the Israelites must live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, and without ephod or idol.

units.leftText: Afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the LORD their God, and David their king, and shall come with trembling to the LORD and to his blessings in the last days.
units.rightText: Afterward, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days.

units.leftText: Hear the LORD’s word, you children of Israel, for the LORD has a charge against the inhabitants of the land: “Indeed there is no truth, nor goodness, nor knowledge of God in the land.
units.rightText: Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the people of the land: “There is no truth, no loving devotion, and no knowledge of God in the land!

units.leftText: There is cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and committing adultery; they break boundaries, and bloodshed causes bloodshed.
units.rightText: Cursing and lying, murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant; one act of bloodshed follows another.

units.leftText: Therefore the land will mourn, and everyone who dwells in it will waste away, with all living things in her, even the animals of the field and the birds of the sky; yes, the fish of the sea also die.
units.rightText: Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it will waste away with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air; even the fish of the sea disappear.

units.leftText: “Yet let no man bring a charge, neither let any man accuse; for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest.
units.rightText: But let no man contend; let no man offer reproof; for your people are like those who contend with a priest.
rightNotes: 4:4 Or for My case is against you, O priests

units.leftText: You will stumble in the day, and the prophet will also stumble with you in the night; and I will destroy your mother.
units.rightText: You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night; so I will destroy your mother —

units.leftText: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you, that you may be no priest to me. Because you have forgotten your God’s law, I will also forget your children.
units.rightText: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your children.

units.leftText: As they were multiplied, so they sinned against me. I will change their glory into shame.
units.rightText: The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; they exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace.
rightNotes: 4:7 Or they exchanged their glorious God (Syriac); MT I will exchange their glory

units.leftText: They feed on the sin of my people, and set their heart on their iniquity.
units.rightText: They feed on the sins of My people and set their hearts on iniquity.
rightNotes: 4:8 Or the sin offerings

units.leftText: It will be like people, like priest; and I will punish them for their ways, and will repay them for their deeds.
units.rightText: And it shall be like people, like priest. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.

units.leftText: They will eat, and not have enough. They will play the prostitute, and will not increase; because they have abandoned listening to the LORD.
units.rightText: They will eat but not be satisfied; they will be promiscuous but not multiply. For they have abandoned the LORD to give themselves

units.leftText: Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away understanding.
units.rightText: to promiscuity, wine, and new wine, which take away understanding.

units.leftText: My people consult with their wooden idol, and answer to a stick of wood. Indeed the spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have been unfaithful to their God.
units.rightText: My people consult their wooden idols, and their divining rods inform them. For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray and they have played the harlot against their God.

units.leftText: They sacrifice on the tops of the mountains, and burn incense on the hills, under oaks, poplars, and terebinths, because its shade is good. Therefore your daughters play the prostitute, and your brides commit adultery.
units.rightText: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. And so your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.

units.leftText: I will not punish your daughters when they play the prostitute, nor your brides when they commit adultery; because the men consort with prostitutes, and they sacrifice with the shrine prostitutes; so the people without understanding will come to ruin.
units.rightText: I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery. For the men themselves go off with prostitutes and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes. So a people without understanding will come to ruin.

units.leftText: “Though you, Israel, play the prostitute, yet don’t let Judah offend; and don’t come to Gilgal, neither go up to Beth Aven, nor swear, ‘As the LORD lives.’
units.rightText: Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, may Judah avoid such guilt! Do not journey to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear on oath, ‘As surely as the LORD lives!’
rightNotes: 4:15 Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29|1KI 12:28-29*.

units.leftText: For Israel has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer. Then how will the LORD feed them like a lamb in a meadow?
units.rightText: For Israel is as obstinate as a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now shepherd them like lambs in an open meadow?

units.leftText: Ephraim is joined to idols. Leave him alone!
units.rightText: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
rightNotes: 4:17 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel

units.leftText: Their drink has become sour. They play the prostitute continually. Her rulers dearly love their shameful way.
units.rightText: When their liquor is gone, they turn to prostitution; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
rightNotes: 4:18 Hebrew her shields

units.leftText: The wind has wrapped her up in its wings; and they shall be disappointed because of their sacrifices.
units.rightText: The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.[’’]
rightNotes: 4:19 Hebrew has wrapped her

units.leftText: “Listen to this, you priests! Listen, house of Israel, and give ear, house of the king! For the judgment is against you; for you have been a snare at Mizpah, and a net spread on Tabor.
units.rightText: “Hear this, O priests! Take heed, O house of Israel! Give ear, O royal house! For this judgment is against you because you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.

units.leftText: The rebels are deep in slaughter, but I discipline all of them.
units.rightText: The rebels are deep in slaughter; but I will chastise them all.

units.leftText: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me; for now, Ephraim, you have played the prostitute. Israel is defiled.
units.rightText: I know all about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me. For now, O Ephraim, you have turned to prostitution; Israel is defiled.
rightNotes: 5:3 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, and 14

units.leftText: Their deeds won’t allow them to turn to their God, for the spirit of prostitution is within them, and they don’t know the LORD.
units.rightText: Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.

units.leftText: The pride of Israel testifies to his face. Therefore Israel and Ephraim will stumble in their iniquity. Judah also will stumble with them.
units.rightText: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity; even Judah stumbles with them.

units.leftText: They will go with their flocks and with their herds to seek the LORD, but they won’t find him. He has withdrawn himself from them.
units.rightText: They go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, but they do not find Him; He has withdrawn Himself from them.

units.leftText: They are unfaithful to the LORD; for they have borne illegitimate children. Now the new moon will devour them with their fields.
units.rightText: They have been unfaithful to the LORD; for they have borne illegitimate children. Now the New Moon will devour them along with their land.
rightNotes: 5:7 Or their New Moon feast or the coming month

units.leftText: “Blow the cornet in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah! Sound a battle cry at Beth Aven, behind you, Benjamin!
units.rightText: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; raise the battle cry in Beth-aven: Lead on, O Benjamin!
rightNotes: 5:8 Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29|1KI 12:28-29*.

units.leftText: Ephraim will become a desolation in the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel, I have made known that which will surely be.
units.rightText: Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.

units.leftText: The princes of Judah are like those who remove a landmark. I will pour out my wrath on them like water.
units.rightText: The princes of Judah are like those who move boundary stones; I will pour out My fury upon them like water.
rightNotes: 5:10 See Proverbs 22:28|PRO 22:28* and Proverbs 23:10.

units.leftText: Ephraim is oppressed, he is crushed in judgment, because he is intent in his pursuit of idols.
units.rightText: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, for he is determined to follow worthless idols.
rightNotes: 5:11 Or to follow human precepts

units.leftText: Therefore I am to Ephraim like a moth, and to the house of Judah like rottenness.
units.rightText: So I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like decay to the house of Judah.

units.leftText: “When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his wound, then Ephraim went to Assyria, and sent to King Jareb: but he is not able to heal you, neither will he cure you of your wound.
units.rightText: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, then Ephraim turned to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot cure you or heal your wound.
rightNotes: 5:13 Or to King Jareb

units.leftText: For I will be to Ephraim like a lion, and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear in pieces and go away. I will carry off, and there will be no one to deliver.
units.rightText: For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear them to pieces and then go away. I will carry them off where no one can rescue them.

units.leftText: I will go and return to my place, until they acknowledge their offense, and seek my face. In their affliction they will seek me earnestly.”
units.rightText: Then I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.”

units.leftText: “Come! Let’s return to the LORD; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds.
units.rightText: Come, let us return to the LORD. For He has torn us to pieces, but He will heal us; He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds.

units.leftText: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
units.rightText: After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live in His presence.

units.leftText: Let’s acknowledge the LORD. Let’s press on to know the LORD. As surely as the sun rises, the LORD will appear. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”
units.rightText: So let us know — let us press on to know the LORD. As surely as the sun rises, He will appear; He will come to us like the rain, like the spring showers that water the earth.

units.leftText: “Ephraim, what shall I do to you? Judah, what shall I do to you? For your love is like a morning cloud, and like the dew that disappears early.
units.rightText: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim ? What shall I do with you, O Judah? For your loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes.
rightNotes: 6:4 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 10

units.leftText: Therefore I have cut them to pieces with the prophets; I killed them with the words of my mouth. Your judgments are like a flash of lightning.
units.rightText: Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth, and My judgments go forth like lightning.

units.leftText: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
units.rightText: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
rightNotes: 6:6 Cited in Matthew 9:13|MAT 9:13* and Matthew 12:7

units.leftText: But they, like Adam, have broken the covenant. They were unfaithful to me there.
units.rightText: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they were unfaithful to Me.
rightNotes: 6:7 Or As at Adam, they have transgressed

units.leftText: Gilead is a city of those who work iniquity; it is stained with blood.
units.rightText: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood.

units.leftText: As gangs of robbers wait to ambush a man, so the company of priests murder on the path toward Shechem, committing shameful crimes.
units.rightText: Like raiders who lie in ambush, so does a band of priests; they murder on the way to Shechem; surely they have committed atrocities.

units.leftText: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing. There is prostitution in Ephraim. Israel is defiled.
units.rightText: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: Ephraim practices prostitution there, and Israel is defiled.

units.leftText: “Also, Judah, there is a harvest appointed for you, when I restore the fortunes of my people.
units.rightText: Also for you, O Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity.
rightNotes: 6:11 Or restore the fortunes of My people

units.leftText: When I would heal Israel, then the iniquity of Ephraim is uncovered, also the wickedness of Samaria; for they commit falsehood, and the thief enters in, and the gang of robbers ravages outside.
units.rightText: When I heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed, as well as the crimes of Samaria. For they practice deceit and thieves break in; bandits raid in the streets.
rightNotes: 7:1 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8 and 11

units.leftText: They don’t consider in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness. Now their own deeds have engulfed them. They are before my face.
units.rightText: But they fail to consider in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds are all around them; they are before My face.

units.leftText: They make the king glad with their wickedness, and the princes with their lies.
units.rightText: They delight the king with their evil, and the princes with their lies.

units.leftText: They are all adulterers. They are burning like an oven that the baker stops stirring, from the kneading of the dough, until it is leavened.
units.rightText: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker who needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough.

units.leftText: On the day of our king, the princes made themselves sick with the heat of wine. He joined his hand with mockers.
units.rightText: The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king; so he joins hands with those who mock him.

units.leftText: For they have prepared their heart like an oven, while they lie in wait. Their anger smolders all night. In the morning it burns as a flaming fire.
units.rightText: For they prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait; all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
rightNotes: 7:6 Literally their baker sleeps

units.leftText: They are all hot as an oven, and devour their judges. All their kings have fallen. There is no one among them who calls to me.
units.rightText: All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings fall; not one of them calls upon Me.

units.leftText: Ephraim mixes himself among the nations. Ephraim is a pancake not turned over.
units.rightText: Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is an unturned cake.

units.leftText: Strangers have devoured his strength, and he doesn’t realize it. Indeed, gray hairs are here and there on him, and he doesn’t realize it.
units.rightText: Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice. Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.

units.leftText: The pride of Israel testifies to his face; yet they haven’t returned to the LORD their God, nor sought him, for all this.
units.rightText: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them, yet they do not return to the LORD their God; despite all this, they do not seek Him.

units.leftText: “Ephraim is like an easily deceived dove, without understanding. They call to Egypt. They go to Assyria.
units.rightText: So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove — calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.

units.leftText: When they go, I will spread my net on them. I will bring them down like the birds of the sky. I will chastise them, as their congregation has heard.
units.rightText: As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the air. I will chastise them when I hear them flocking together.
rightNotes: 7:12 Or I will chastise them according to what was reported against them in the assembly.

units.leftText: Woe to them! For they have wandered from me. Destruction to them! For they have trespassed against me. Though I would redeem them, yet they have spoken lies against me.
units.rightText: Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me! Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.

units.leftText: They haven’t cried to me with their heart, but they howl on their beds. They assemble themselves for grain and new wine. They turn away from me.
units.rightText: They do not cry out to Me from their hearts when they wail upon their beds. They slash themselves for grain and new wine, but turn away from Me.
rightNotes: 7:14 Some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX; see 1 Kings 18:28|1KI 18:28*. Most Hebrew manuscripts They gather together

units.leftText: Though I have taught and strengthened their arms, yet they plot evil against me.
units.rightText: Although I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against Me.

units.leftText: They return, but not to the Most High. They are like a faulty bow. Their princes will fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue. This will be their derision in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue; for this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: “Put the trumpet to your lips! Something like an eagle is over the LORD’s house, because they have broken my covenant and rebelled against my law.
units.rightText: Put the ram’s horn to your lips! An eagle looms over the house of the LORD, because the people have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law.

units.leftText: They cry to me, ‘My God, we, Israel, acknowledge you!’
units.rightText: Israel cries out to Me, “O our God, we know You!”

units.leftText: Israel has cast off that which is good. The enemy will pursue him.
units.rightText: But Israel has rejected good; an enemy will pursue him.

units.leftText: They have set up kings, but not by me. They have made princes, and I didn’t approve. Of their silver and their gold they have made themselves idols, that they may be cut off.
units.rightText: They set up kings, but not by Me. They make princes, but without My approval. With their silver and gold they make themselves idols, to their own destruction.

units.leftText: Let Samaria throw out his calf idol! My anger burns against them! How long will it be until they are capable of purity?
units.rightText: He has rejected your calf, O Samaria. My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
rightNotes: 8:5 Or calf idol; see 1 Kings 12:29|1KI 12:29*.

units.leftText: For this is even from Israel! The workman made it, and it is no God; indeed, the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.
units.rightText: For this thing is from Israel— a craftsman made it, and it is not God. It will be broken to pieces, that calf of Samaria.

units.leftText: For they sow the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind. He has no standing grain. The stalk will yield no head. If it does yield, strangers will swallow it up.
units.rightText: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind. There is no standing grain; what sprouts fails to yield flour. Even if it should produce, the foreigners would swallow it up.

units.leftText: Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a worthless thing.
units.rightText: Israel is swallowed up! Now they are among the nations like a worthless vessel.

units.leftText: For they have gone up to Assyria, like a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has hired lovers for himself.
units.rightText: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.
rightNotes: 8:9 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 11

units.leftText: But although they sold themselves among the nations, I will now gather them; and they begin to waste away because of the oppression of the king of mighty ones.
units.rightText: Though they hire allies among the nations, I will now round them up, and they will begin to diminish under the oppression of the king of princes.

units.leftText: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, they became for him altars for sinning.
units.rightText: Though Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin, they became his altars for sinning.

units.leftText: I wrote for him the many things of my law, but they were regarded as a strange thing.
units.rightText: Though I wrote for them the great things of My law, they regarded them as something strange.

units.leftText: As for the sacrifices of my offerings, they sacrifice meat and eat it, but the LORD doesn’t accept them. Now he will remember their iniquity, and punish their sins. They will return to Egypt.
units.rightText: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, and though they eat the meat, the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.

units.leftText: For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; but I will send a fire on his cities, and it will devour its fortresses.”
units.rightText: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has multiplied its fortified cities. But I will send fire upon their cities, and it will consume their citadels.

units.leftText: Don’t rejoice, Israel, to jubilation like the nations; for you were unfaithful to your God. You love the wages of a prostitute at every grain threshing floor.
units.rightText: Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations, for you have played the harlot against your God; you have made love for hire on every threshing floor.

units.leftText: The threshing floor and the wine press won’t feed them, and the new wine will fail her.
units.rightText: The threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them.

units.leftText: They won’t dwell in the LORD’s land; but Ephraim will return to Egypt, and they will eat unclean food in Assyria.
units.rightText: They will not remain in the land of the LORD; Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.
rightNotes: 9:3 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; similarly in verses 8, 11, 13, and 16

units.leftText: They won’t pour out wine offerings to the LORD, neither will they be pleasing to him. Their sacrifices will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat of it will be polluted; for their bread will be for their appetite. It will not come into the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please Him, but will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled. For their bread will be for themselves; it will not enter the house of the LORD.

units.leftText: What will you do in the day of solemn assembly, and in the day of the feast of the LORD?
units.rightText: What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?

units.leftText: For, behold, when they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them up. Memphis will bury them. Nettles will possess their pleasant things of silver. Thorns will be in their tents.
units.rightText: For even if they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. Their precious silver will be taken over by thistles, and thorns will overrun their tents.

units.leftText: The days of visitation have come. The days of reckoning have come. Israel will consider the prophet to be a fool, and the man who is inspired to be insane, because of the abundance of your sins, and because your hostility is great.
units.rightText: The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived — let Israel know it. The prophet is called a fool, and the inspired man insane, because of the greatness of your iniquity and hostility.

units.leftText: A prophet watches over Ephraim with my God. A fowler’s snare is on all of his paths, and hostility in the house of his God.
units.rightText: The prophet is Ephraim’s watchman, along with my God, yet the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths. Hostility is in the house of his God!
rightNotes: 9:8 Or The prophet is the watchman over Ephraim, the people of my God

units.leftText: They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their iniquity. He will punish them for their sins.
units.rightText: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their guilt; He will punish their sins.

units.leftText: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the first ripe in the fig tree at its first season; but they came to Baal Peor, and consecrated themselves to the shameful thing, and became abominable like that which they loved.
units.rightText: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the firstfruits of the fig tree in its first season. But they went to Baal-peor, and consecrated themselves to Shame; so they became as detestable as the thing they loved.

units.leftText: As for Ephraim, their glory will fly away like a bird. There will be no birth, no one with child, and no conception.
units.rightText: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.

units.leftText: Though they bring up their children, yet I will bereave them, so that not a man shall be left. Indeed, woe also to them when I depart from them!
units.rightText: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them of each one. Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!

units.leftText: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place; but Ephraim will bring out his children to the murderer.
units.rightText: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a meadow. But Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.

units.leftText: Give them—LORD what will you give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
units.rightText: Give them, O LORD— what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that dry up!

units.leftText: “All their wickedness is in Gilgal; for there I hated them. Because of the wickedness of their deeds, I will drive them out of my house! I will love them no more. All their princes are rebels.
units.rightText: All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them. I will drive them from My house for the wickedness of their deeds. I will no longer love them; all their leaders are rebellious.

units.leftText: Ephraim is struck. Their root has dried up. They will bear no fruit. Even though they give birth, yet I will kill the beloved ones of their womb.”
units.rightText: Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered; they cannot bear fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay the darlings of their wombs.

units.leftText: My God will cast them away, because they didn’t listen to him; and they will be wanderers among the nations.
units.rightText: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations.

units.leftText: Israel is a luxuriant vine that produces his fruit. According to the abundance of his fruit he has multiplied his altars. As their land has prospered, they have adorned their sacred stones.
units.rightText: Israel was a luxuriant vine, yielding fruit for himself. The more his fruit increased, the more he increased the altars. The better his land produced, the better he made the sacred pillars.

units.leftText: Their heart is divided. Now they will be found guilty. He will demolish their altars. He will destroy their sacred stones.
units.rightText: Their hearts are devious; now they must bear their guilt. The LORD will break down their altars and demolish their sacred pillars.

units.leftText: Surely now they will say, “We have no king; for we don’t fear the LORD; and the king, what can he do for us?”
units.rightText: Surely now they will say, “We have no king, for we do not revere the LORD. What can a king do for us?”

units.leftText: They make promises, swearing falsely in making covenants. Therefore judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of the field.
units.rightText: They speak mere words; with false oaths they make covenants. So judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.

units.leftText: The inhabitants of Samaria will be in terror for the calves of Beth Aven, for its people will mourn over it, along with its priests who rejoiced over it, for its glory, because it has departed from it.
units.rightText: The people of Samaria will fear for the calf of Beth-aven. Indeed, its people will mourn over it with its idolatrous priests — those who rejoiced in its glory — for it has been taken from them into exile.
rightNotes: 10:5 Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29|1KI 12:28-29*.

units.leftText: It also will be carried to Assyria for a present to a great king. Ephraim will receive shame, and Israel will be ashamed of his own counsel.
units.rightText: Yes, it will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will be seized with shame; Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.
rightNotes: 10:6 Or to King Jareb
10:6 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 11
10:6 Or of its own counsel

units.leftText: Samaria and her king float away like a twig on the water.
units.rightText: Samaria will be carried off with her king like a twig on the surface of the water.

units.leftText: The high places also of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. The thorn and the thistle will come up on their altars. They will tell the mountains, “Cover us!” and the hills, “Fall on us!”
units.rightText: The high places of Aven will be destroyed— it is the sin of Israel; thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!”
rightNotes: 10:8 Or of wickedness; Aven is a reference to Beth-aven (a derogatory term for Bethel); see verse 5.
10:8 Cited in Luke 23:30|LUK 23:30*; see also Revelation 6:16.

units.leftText: “Israel, you have sinned from the days of Gibeah. There they remained. The battle against the children of iniquity doesn’t overtake them in Gibeah.
units.rightText: Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel, and there you have remained. Did not the battle in Gibeah overtake the sons of iniquity?
rightNotes: 10:9 Or Did not the battle overtake the sons of iniquity in Gibeah?

units.leftText: When it is my desire, I will chastise them; and the nations will be gathered against them when they are bound to their two transgressions.
units.rightText: I will chasten them when I please; nations will be gathered against them to put them in bondage for their double transgression.

units.leftText: Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh, so I will put a yoke on her beautiful neck. I will set a rider on Ephraim. Judah will plow. Jacob will break his clods.
units.rightText: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh; but I will place a yoke on her fair neck. I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow, and Jacob will break the hard ground.

units.leftText: Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap according to kindness. Break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
units.rightText: Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground. For it is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain.

units.leftText: You have plowed wickedness. You have reaped iniquity. You have eaten the fruit of lies, for you trusted in your way, in the multitude of your mighty men.
units.rightText: You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you have trusted in your own way and in the multitude of your mighty men,

units.leftText: Therefore a battle roar will arise among your people, and all your fortresses will be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel in the day of battle. The mother was dashed in pieces with her children.
units.rightText: the roar of battle will rise against your people, so that all your fortresses will be demolished as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel in the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces along with their children.

units.leftText: So Bethel will do to you because of your great wickedness. At daybreak the king of Israel will be destroyed.
units.rightText: Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel, because of your great wickedness. When the day dawns, the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.

units.leftText: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
units.rightText: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.
rightNotes: 11:1 Cited in Matthew 2:15|MAT 2:15*

units.leftText: They called to them, so they went from them. They sacrificed to the Baals, and burned incense to engraved images.
units.rightText: But the more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
rightNotes: 11:2 LXX; Hebrew The more they called them, the more they went from them.

units.leftText: Yet I taught Ephraim to walk. I took them by their arms, but they didn’t know that I healed them.
units.rightText: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms, but they never realized that it was I who healed them.
rightNotes: 11:3 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8, 9, and 12

units.leftText: I drew them with cords of a man, with ties of love; and I was to them like those who lift up the yoke on their necks; and I bent down to him and I fed him.
units.rightText: I led them with cords of kindness, with ropes of love; I lifted the yoke from their necks and bent down to feed them.

units.leftText: “They won’t return into the land of Egypt; but the Assyrian will be their king, because they refused to repent.
units.rightText: Will they not return to the land of Egypt and be ruled by Assyria because they refused to repent?

units.leftText: The sword will fall on their cities, and will destroy the bars of their gates, and will put an end to their plans.
units.rightText: A sword will flash through their cities; it will destroy the bars of their gates and consume them in their own plans.

units.leftText: My people are determined to turn from me. Though they call to the Most High, he certainly won’t exalt them.
units.rightText: My people are bent on turning from Me. Though they call to the Most High, He will by no means exalt them. God’s Love for Israel

units.leftText: “How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I make you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within me, my compassion is aroused.
units.rightText: How could I give you up, O Ephraim? How could I surrender you, O Israel? How could I make you like Admah? How could I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within Me; My compassion is stirred!

units.leftText: I will not execute the fierceness of my anger. I will not return to destroy Ephraim, for I am God, and not man—the Holy One among you. I will not come in wrath.
units.rightText: I will not execute the full fury of My anger; I will not destroy Ephraim again. For I am God and not man — the Holy One among you — and I will not come in wrath.

units.leftText: They will walk after the LORD, who will roar like a lion; for he will roar, and the children will come trembling from the west.
units.rightText: They will walk after the LORD; He will roar like a lion. When He roars, His children will come trembling from the west.

units.leftText: They will come trembling like a bird out of Egypt, and like a dove out of the land of Assyria; and I will settle them in their houses,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria. Then I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.

units.leftText: Ephraim surrounds me with falsehood, and the house of Israel with deceit. Judah still strays from God, and is unfaithful to the Holy One.
units.rightText: Ephraim surrounds Me with lies, the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.
rightNotes: 11:12 Or and Judah is unruly against God, the faithful Holy One

units.leftText: Ephraim feeds on wind, and chases the east wind. He continually multiplies lies and desolation. They make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried into Egypt.
units.rightText: Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day long; he multiplies lies and violence; he makes a covenant with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt.
rightNotes: 12:1 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8 and 14

units.leftText: The LORD also has a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds he will repay him.
units.rightText: The LORD has a charge to bring against Judah. He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
rightNotes: 12:2 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.

units.leftText: In the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his manhood he contended with God.
units.rightText: In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel, and in his vigor he wrestled with God.

units.leftText: Indeed, he struggled with the angel, and prevailed; he wept, and made supplication to him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us—
units.rightText: Yes, he struggled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought His favor; he found Him at Bethel and spoke with Him there —
rightNotes: 12:4 Or Angel
12:4 LXX and Syriac; MT and there He spoke with us

units.leftText: even the LORD, the God of Armies. The LORD is his name of renown!
units.rightText: the LORD God of Hosts, the LORD is His name of renown.

units.leftText: Therefore turn to your God. Keep kindness and justice, and wait continually for your God.
units.rightText: But you must return to your God; maintain love and justice, and always wait on your God.

units.leftText: A merchant has dishonest scales in his hand. He loves to defraud.
units.rightText: A merchant loves to defraud with dishonest scales in his hands.

units.leftText: Ephraim said, “Surely I have become rich. I have found myself wealth. In all my wealth they won’t find in me any iniquity that is sin.”
units.rightText: And Ephraim boasts: “How rich I have become! I have found wealth for myself. In all my labors, they can find in me no iniquity that is sinful.”

units.leftText: “But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. I will yet again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the solemn feast.
units.rightText: But I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt. I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.

units.leftText: I have also spoken to the prophets, and I have multiplied visions; and by the ministry of the prophets I have used parables.
units.rightText: I spoke through the prophets and multiplied their visions; I gave parables through the prophets.

units.leftText: If Gilead is wicked, surely they are worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls. Indeed, their altars are like heaps in the furrows of the field.
units.rightText: Is there iniquity in Gilead? They will surely come to nothing. Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Indeed, their altars will be heaps of stones in the furrows of the field.

units.leftText: Jacob fled into the country of Aram. Israel served to get a wife. For a wife he tended flocks and herds.
units.rightText: Jacob fled to the land of Aram and Israel worked for a wife — for a wife he tended sheep.
rightNotes: 12:12 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.
units.rightText: But by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.

units.leftText: Ephraim has bitterly provoked anger. Therefore his blood will be left on him, and his Lord will repay his contempt.
units.rightText: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger, so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and repay him for his contempt.

units.leftText: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling. He exalted himself in Israel, but when he became guilty through Baal, he died.
units.rightText: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he incurred guilt through Baal, and he died.
rightNotes: 13:1 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 12

units.leftText: Now they sin more and more, and have made themselves molten images of their silver, even idols according to their own understanding, all of them the work of the craftsmen. They say of them, ‘They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves.’
units.rightText: Now they sin more and more and make for themselves cast images, idols skillfully made from their silver, all of them the work of craftsmen. People say of them, “They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves!”
rightNotes: 13:2 Or “The men who sacrifice kiss the calves!”See 1 Kings 19:18|1KI 19:18*.

units.leftText: Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the dew that passes away early, like the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the threshing floor, and like the smoke out of the chimney.
units.rightText: Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, like smoke through an open window.

units.leftText: “Yet I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; and you shall acknowledge no god but me, and besides me there is no savior.
units.rightText: Yet I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me.

units.leftText: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of great drought.
units.rightText: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.

units.leftText: According to their pasture, so were they filled; they were filled, and their heart was exalted. Therefore they have forgotten me.
units.rightText: When they had pasture, they became satisfied; when they were satisfied, their hearts became proud, and as a result they forgot Me.

units.leftText: Therefore I am like a lion to them. Like a leopard, I will lurk by the path.
units.rightText: So like a lion I will pounce on them; like a leopard I will lurk by the path.

units.leftText: I will meet them like a bear that is bereaved of her cubs, and will tear the covering of their heart. There I will devour them like a lioness. The wild animal will tear them.
units.rightText: Like a bear robbed of her cubs I will attack them, and I will tear open their chests. There I will devour them like a lion, like a wild beast tearing them apart. Death and Resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:50–58|1CO 15:50-58*)

units.leftText: You are destroyed, Israel, because you are against me, against your helper.
units.rightText: You are destroyed, O Israel, because you are against Me — against your helper.

units.leftText: Where is your king now, that he may save you in all your cities? And your judges, of whom you said, ‘Give me a king and princes’?
units.rightText: Where is your king now to save you in all your cities, and the rulers to whom you said, “Give me a king and princes”?
rightNotes: 13:10 Or Shall I be your King now

units.leftText: I have given you a king in my anger, and have taken him away in my wrath.
units.rightText: So in My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.

units.leftText: The guilt of Ephraim is stored up. His sin is stored up.
units.rightText: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up.

units.leftText: The sorrows of a travailing woman will come on him. He is an unwise son, for when it is time, he doesn’t come to the opening of the womb.
units.rightText: Labor pains come upon him, but he is an unwise son. When the time arrives, he fails to present himself at the opening of the womb.

units.leftText: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol. I will redeem them from death! Death, where are your plagues? Sheol, where is your destruction? “Compassion will be hidden from my eyes.
units.rightText: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death. Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting? Compassion is hidden from My eyes. Judgment on Samaria
leftNotes: 13:14 Sheol is the place of the dead.
rightNotes: 13:14 Or Shall I ransom them from the power of Sheol? Shall I redeem them from Death?
13:14 LXX Where, O Death, is your penalty? Where, O Hades, is your sting?Cited in 1 Corinthians 15:55|1CO 15:55*

units.leftText: Though he is fruitful among his brothers, an east wind will come, the breath of the LORD coming up from the wilderness; and his spring will become dry, and his fountain will be dried up. He will plunder the storehouse of treasure.
units.rightText: Although he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come — a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert. His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry. The wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.

units.leftText: Samaria will bear her guilt, for she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword. Their infants will be dashed in pieces, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.”
units.rightText: Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.

units.leftText: Israel, return to the LORD your God; for you have fallen because of your sin.
units.rightText: Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled by your iniquity.

units.leftText: Take words with you, and return to the LORD. Tell him, “Forgive all our sins, and accept that which is good; so we offer bulls as we vowed of our lips.
units.rightText: Bring your confessions and return to the LORD. Say to Him: “Take away all our iniquity and receive us graciously, that we may present the fruit of our lips.
rightNotes: 14:2 LXX and Syriac; Hebrew that we may present our lips as sacrificial bulls

units.leftText: Assyria can’t save us. We won’t ride on horses; neither will we say any more to the work of our hands, ‘Our gods!’ for in you the fatherless finds mercy.”
units.rightText: Assyria will not save us, nor will we ride on horses. We will never again say, ‘Our gods!’ to the work of our own hands. For in You the fatherless find compassion.” A Promise of God’s Blessing

units.leftText: “I will heal their waywardness. I will love them freely; for my anger is turned away from them.
units.rightText: I will heal their apostasy; I will freely love them, for My anger has turned away from them.

units.leftText: I will be like the dew to Israel. He will blossom like the lily, and send down his roots like Lebanon.
units.rightText: I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily and take root like the cedars of Lebanon.

units.leftText: His branches will spread, and his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.
units.rightText: His shoots will sprout, and his splendor will be like the olive tree, his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon.

units.leftText: Men will dwell in his shade. They will revive like the grain, and blossom like the vine. Their fragrance will be like the wine of Lebanon.
units.rightText: They will return and dwell in his shade; they will grow grain and blossom like the vine. His renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.

units.leftText: Ephraim, what have I to do any more with idols? I answer, and will take care of him. I am like a green cypress tree; from me your fruit is found.”
units.rightText: O Ephraim, what have I to do anymore with idols? It is I who answer and watch over him. I am like a flourishing cypress; your fruit comes from Me.
rightNotes: 14:8 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel
14:8 Or pine or juniper or fir

units.leftText: Who is wise, that he may understand these things? Who is prudent, that he may know them? For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them, but the rebellious stumble in them.
units.rightText: Whoever is wise, let him understand these things; whoever is discerning, let him know them. For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them but the rebellious stumble in them.
